title: Television and family demography: Evidence from a natural experiment in East Germany
treatment: residence-based ability to receive Western television in the GDR
outcome: marriage, childbirth, divorce; family attitudes
reason: Signal-geography natural experiment within one economy attributes reduced marriage and childbearing to Western TV role models via attitude change.

title: Responsibility, social aspirations, and contemporary low fertility: a case study of rural West Bengal, India
authors: Kakoli Das; Saswata Ghosh; Mary K. Shenk
treatment: aspirational model of responsible, heavily investing parenthood held by rural parents
outcome: very low realized fertility and small-family motivation
reason: Ideal of investing heavily in few children drives sub-replacement fertility in a rural, economically insecure setting where structural development has not moved.

title: Television and fertility: evidence from a natural experiment
treatment: topography-driven access to West German television promoting one/no-child families
outcome: individual and aggregate fertility in East Germany
reason: Natural experiment isolating exposure to a Western small-family model within a single economy, with the effect attributed to depicted role models.

title: The Fall in Global Fertility: A Quantitative Model
treatment: externally funded population-policy effort acting on family-size social norms
outcome: fertility rates in middle- and low-income countries
reason: Quantitative model simulates the norm-shifting channel of development-institution population programmes separately from human capital, income, and contraceptive access.

title: Marital Processes, Arranged Marriage, and Contraception to Limit Fertility
authors: Dirgha J. Ghimire; William G. Axinn
treatment: participation in spouse choice versus familially arranged marriage
outcome: contraception to terminate childbearing
reason: Spread of the conjugal marriage form through rural Asia as a determinant of long-term fertility limitation, estimated net of the contemporaneous social changes that shape both.

title: Fertility, electricity and television: is there a link? Evidence from Pakistan, 1990–2018
authors: Luca Tasciotti; Farooq Sulehria; Natascha Wagner
treatment: household television access, electrification, and soap-opera content in Pakistan
outcome: fertility rates, 1990-2018
reason: TV access reduces fertility with the effect attributed to soap-opera role models and household forms, though wealth/education adjustment is covariate control rather than design.

title: A Cautionary Tale of Evaluating Identifying Assumptions: Did Reality TV Really Cause a Decline in Teenage Childbearing?
authors: David A. Jaeger; Theodore Joyce; Robert Kaestner
treatment: exposure to MTV's '16 and Pregnant' via pre-treatment MTV viewership across media markets
outcome: teen birth rates
reason: Re-examination of a televised family-model depiction on teen childbearing; dual-home media case tagged shared with A.20.

title: All You Need is Cable TV?
treatment: arrival of cable television in rural Indian villages
outcome: fertility, tolerance of spousal violence, son preference, women's autonomy
reason: Replication of a cable-TV introduction design attributing fertility and gender-attitude change to televised depictions of modern family life; channel reading equally live.

title: Does Electrification Spur the Fertility Transition? Evidence From Indonesia
authors: Michael Grimm; Robert Sparrow; Luca Tasciotti
treatment: electrification-induced exposure to television
outcome: fertility preferences and realized fertility decline
reason: television exposure identified as a key channel to fertility preferences and births; channel and depicted-model readings both live

title: The impact of television and radio on reproductive behavior and on HIV / AIDS knowledge and behavior.
authors: Charles F. Westoff; Dawn Koffman; Caroline Moreau
treatment: frequency of television and radio exposure across 48 developing countries
outcome: contraceptive use, desired number of children, recent births
reason: Media exposure framed as a window onto modern life competing with traditional marriage and childbearing values, with associations persisting net of schooling, wealth and urban residence; channel reading equally live so shared with A.20.

title: The Association of Television and Radio with Reproductive Behavior
treatment: frequency of television and radio exposure
outcome: contraceptive use, desired number of children, recent fertility
reason: Media exposure across 48 developing countries linked to fertility and desired family size, with the effect attributed to depicted modern-family life; content unmeasured so the channel reading is equally live.

title: The Multifaceted Impact of Education on Fertility: Unpacking the “BASIC” Effects in China
treatment: years of education, instrumented, decomposed into base/ambition/spouse/income/concept channels
outcome: number of children, parity progression, fertility intentions
reason: Design explicitly separates a 'concept' (ideational) channel of schooling from income and work-status returns (Wall 5)

title: Education and Fertility in Sub-Saharan Africa: Individual and Community Effects
treatment: community average education level, net of a woman's own education
outcome: woman's birth rates
reason: Aggregate schooling spillover onto women whose own education did not change — Caldwell's mass-education mechanism, net of own education and urbanization (Wall 5).

title: The importance of education for fertility in Sub-Saharan Africa is substantially underestimated when community effects are ignored
treatment: community (cluster) mean schooling, holding own schooling constant
outcome: birth hazards / fertility
reason: Estimates schooling spillovers onto women whose own education did not change, net of urbanization — the design isolates a non-individual, non-wage schooling channel.

title: Mass Education and Fertility Transition
authors: William G. Axinn; Jennifer S. Barber
treatment: childhood proximity to a school in rural Nepal
outcome: permanent contraceptive use / fertility limitation
reason: School-proximity effect estimated net of own, husband's, and children's schooling, isolating exposure for people whose own schooling did not change.

title: A search for aggregate-level effects of education on fertility, using data from Zimbabwe
treatment: district-level average schooling and literacy, net of own education
outcome: birth hazards, fertility desires, contraceptive use
reason: Estimates aggregate education spillovers on women whose own schooling did not change, controlling own education and urbanization — the ideational-content design of Wall 5.

title: Harmony in diplomacy, convergence in choices: Low fertility diffusion through Sino‐Korean normalization
treatment: 1992 Sino-Korean diplomatic normalization opening contact with low-fertility South Korea
outcome: fertility and marriage rates among Korean Chinese
reason: Contact with an external modern reference society is the exposure, with adoption of its low-fertility norms as the stated mechanism.

title: International migration and the advent of a new demographic era
treatment: destination-country fertility, girls' enrolment and gender equity along migration corridors
outcome: TFR in high-fertility origin countries
reason: Tests transmission of destination family and gender norms to origin fertility via migration corridors; bivariate correlations only.

title: Fertility of immigrants and their descendants in Spain: intergenerational convergence to the native population’s behaviour?
authors: Jesús García-Gómez; Alberto Del Rey; Mikołaj Stanek
treatment: immigrant generation and age at arrival in Spain (exposure to host society)
outcome: fertility level relative to natives
reason: Estimand is intergenerational convergence to native fertility with exposure, tested against socialization hypotheses (Wall 2 migrant seam).

title: Competing Family Pathways for Immigrants and Their Descendants in Germany
treatment: immigrant generation and origin-group exposure to German host family norms
outcome: cohabitation, marriage, first birth
reason: Event-history study of convergence with native partnership and fertility pathways across migrant generations and cohorts.

title: Population Control Policies and Fertility Convergence
treatment: externally propelled global population-control programmes aimed at changing family-size norms
outcome: national fertility rates and convergence
reason: Western-elite-originated development programmes altering family-size norms are argued to drive fertility convergence despite large differences in GDP, education, urbanization, and female employment.

title: Immigration to the UK from High‐Fertility Countries: Intergenerational Adaptation and Fertility Convergence
treatment: immigrant generation / duration of exposure to UK host society
outcome: period TFR and completed fertility by ethnic group and generation
reason: Estimand is intergenerational adaptation and convergence on host childbearing norms with exposure, the migrant-seam case assigned to D.1.b.

title: The impact of outmigration of men on fertility and marriage in the migrant-sending states of Mexico, 1995–2000
treatment: municipal level of male outmigration to the US
outcome: total fertility and proportion of women married
reason: Migration exposure associated with marriage decline net of sex ratio and education, attributed to changing family-formation ideas.

title: Community Context, Land Use, and First Birth
authors: Dirgha J. Ghimire; William G. Axinn
treatment: childhood and adult proximity to non-family services and institutions in rural Nepal
outcome: monthly odds of first birth
reason: Exposure to modern non-family institutions said to spread new expectations about family life, estimated on first-birth timing against agricultural child-labour returns

title: Fertility attitudes and behavior of Saudi Arabian students enrolled in U.S. universities
authors: Khalid A. A. Al‐Mubarak; Donald J. Adamchak
treatment: length of stay studying in U.S. universities
outcome: fertility attitudes and number of children
reason: Direct residence in a Western setting is among the modelled determinants of fertility attitudes and behaviour among Saudi nationals.

title: Assimilation, Disruption and the Fertility of Mexican-Origin Women in the United States <sup/>
authors: Elizabeth Hervey Stephen; Frank D. Bean
treatment: length of familial exposure to the United States (nativity, generation, period of immigration)
outcome: current and cumulative fertility of Mexican-origin women
reason: Migrant-seam case on the convergence-with-exposure side: fertility declines with duration and generation of US exposure, not persistence of origin norms.

title: Rural Income‐Generating Programs and Fertility Limitation: Evidence from a Microdemographic Study in Nepal<sup>1</sup>
treatment: participation in rural development programs organizing cooperative groups
outcome: contraceptive use to limit fertility
reason: Exposure to development-programme institutions as a determinant of fertility limitation in Nepal, though the stated mechanism runs partly through childbearing costs.

title: Family organization and fertility limitation in Nepal
treatment: premarital experience in nonfamily institutions (schooling, wage work, travel) for wives and husbands
outcome: adoption of fertility limitation
reason: Exposure to nonfamily institutions carrying a new family mode of organization predicts fertility limitation in transitional Nepal.
